summary: This note is the Snowflake documentation page for the VALIDATE_PIPE_LOAD table function, which returns details about errors Snowpipe encountered when loading data files into Snowflake tables. It covers the syntax with required PIPE_NAME and START_TIME and optional END_TIME arguments, the privileges needed (pipe ownership, MONITOR, or MONITOR EXECUTION, plus stage and table privileges), and the output columns such as ERROR, FILE, LINE, and REJECTED_RECORD. Key limits are that it only covers the last 14 days, returns nothing when no errors occurred, and returns a user error for pipes using COPY transformations. The note also includes a one-hour example query.
one_line: Snowflake table function VALIDATE_PIPE_LOAD that returns error details for Snowpipe data loads over the last 14 days.
key_facts: VALIDATE_PIPE_LOAD is a table function used to validate data files processed by Snowpipe.
The function returns details about any errors encountered during an attempted data load into Snowflake tables.
The function returns pipe activity within the last 14 days.
The syntax requires PIPE_NAME => '<string>' and START_TIME => <constant_expr>, with END_TIME as an optional argument.
START_TIME and END_TIME are timestamps in TIMESTAMP_LTZ format and must be within the last 14 days.
Results are returned only for the pipe owner or a role with the OWNERSHIP privilege on the pipe, or a role with MONITOR on the pipe or the global MONITOR EXECUTION privilege.
If Snowpipe encountered no errors within the specified time range, the function returns no results.
If the COPY statement in the pipe includes a COPY transformation, the function currently returns a user error.
If the specified date range falls outside the last 15 days, an error is returned.
Output columns include ERROR, FILE, LINE, CHARACTER, BYTE_OFFSET, CATEGORY, CODE, SQL_STATE, COLUMN_NAME, ROW_NUMBER, ROW_START_LINE and REJECTED_RECORD.
The ERROR column shows the first error in the source file, and FILE gives the name of the source file where the error was encountered.
The example validates loads for the MY_DB.PUBLIC.MYPIPE pipe within the previous hour using dateadd(hour, -1, current_timestamp()).
USAGE on an external stage or READ on an internal stage is needed in the pipe definition, along with SELECT and INSERT on the target table.
